sentences.show: For 133 days, he drifted alone across the Atlantic, on a raft smaller than a car.
His name was Poon Lim, a young steward from China, on a British cargo ship.
In November 1942, a German submarine hit her with two torpedoes. She sank in two minutes.
Poon was thrown into the sea. The U-boat crew saw him. They laughed, and waved him away.
After two hours in the water, he found an empty life raft.
It had water and biscuits. Enough for weeks. Not months.
When the food ran out, he made a fish hook from the spring of a flashlight.
He caught fish and seabirds, and dried their meat in the sun.
When the rain stopped, he caught a shark, beat it to death, and drank the blood from its liver.
Ships passed him by. A Navy plane spotted him, then a storm hid him again.
He stopped counting days, and started counting full moons.
In April 1943, three Brazilian fishermen found him, close to the shore.
He was the only survivor of his ship.
The King gave him a medal, and the Royal Navy put his tricks into its survival manuals.
Told that no one had ever survived longer on a raft, he said: "I hope no one will ever have to break that record."
Poon Lim kept counting the moons. Keep counting the stories with us. Subscribe.
